items.title: Top 5 Heaviest Objects in the Solar System (Earth Doesn't Make It) #shorts
items.description:
The five heaviest objects in the solar system, weighed in Earths and counted down from #5 to #1.
Full video: What If Jupiter Became a Star? It Would Need 80 Jupiters

Sources
• NASA planetary fact sheets (NSSDC): masses Uranus 86.8, Neptune 102.4, Saturn 568.3, Jupiter 1,898 × 10^24 kg; Earth 5.97 × 10^24 kg; Sun 1,988,400 × 10^24 kg (332,946 Earths)
• NASA: the Sun holds about 99.86% of the solar system's mass; Saturn's mean density 0.687 g/cm³ (less than water); Uranus's axis is tilted about 98°
• NASA: Neptune is smaller in diameter than Uranus (49,528 vs 51,118 km) but more massive
• Own calculations: Jupiter ÷ all other planets combined = 317.8 ÷ 128.8 Earth masses ≈ 2.5

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.

items.title: What If We Swapped the Sun for 5 Other Stars? One Puts Earth INSIDE It
items.description:
Keep Earth exactly where it is and swap the Sun for five real stars: Proxima Centauri, Alpha Centauri A, Sirius A, Sirius B and Stephenson 2-18. What the noon sky would look like, how warm Earth would get, and where a planet would need to be to stay like home. Spoiler: one of them puts Earth inside the star.

Chapters
0:00 Same Earth, different star
0:30 The rules of the swap
0:51 Swap 1: Proxima Centauri (the air freezes)
2:32 Swap 2: Alpha Centauri A (the Sun's near-twin)
3:36 Swap 3: Sirius A (25 times brighter)
4:47 Swap 4: Sirius B (a dead star smaller than Earth)
6:00 Swap 5: Stephenson 2-18 (Earth inside a star)
7:31 Five swaps, zero winners
8:15 Next episode

Sources
• Proxima Centauri: radius 0.154 solar radii, mass 0.122 solar masses, luminosity about 0.0016 of the Sun, surface about 3,000 K, distance 4.24 light-years (ESO; Ribas et al. 2017; Wikipedia summary of published values)
• Proxima b: orbital period 11.2 days, about 0.049 AU from its star (Anglada-Escudé et al. 2016, Nature)
• MacGregor et al. (2021), Astrophysical Journal Letters: a 2019 flare on Proxima Centauri brightened about 14,000 times in far-ultraviolet light within seconds
• Alpha Centauri A: radius 1.22 solar radii, mass about 1.1 solar masses, luminosity about 1.52 suns, surface about 5,790 K, distance 4.37 light-years (Kervella et al. 2017, VLTI/PIONIER)
• Sirius A: radius 1.71 solar radii, mass 2.06 solar masses, luminosity about 25 suns, surface about 9,900 K; Sirius B: white dwarf, about 1.02 solar masses, radius about 0.0081 solar radii (0.88 Earth radii), surface about 25,000 K, luminosity about 0.056 suns; distance 8.6 light-years (Bond et al. 2017, HST astrometry)
• Stephenson 2-18: estimated radius about 2,150 solar radii; luminosity estimates from about 90,000 to 630,000 suns (440,000 used here); distance about 19,000 light-years; both depend on its assumed membership in the Stephenson 2 cluster
• Kopparapu et al. (2013), Astrophysical Journal: conservative habitable zone for the Sun about 0.99 to 1.70 AU; runaway greenhouse at about 6% more sunlight than Earth receives today
• NASA: about three out of four stars in the Milky Way are red dwarfs; the Sun is about 4.6 billion years old
• Nitrogen freezes at about −210 °C; lead melts at 327 °C; Venus's average surface temperature about 464 °C (NASA)
• Own calculations (Python): average temperature = 288 K × (luminosity)^0.25 at Earth's distance, keeping the same air and clouds (a simple estimate, not a climate model); Earth-like zone scaled by the square root of luminosity; year at 1 AU = 1/√(mass); disc size = radius × 0.533°; Stephenson 2-18 radius = 10.0 AU; light travel time to 663 AU = 3.8 days

—

items.title: This Star Is Smaller Than Earth. It Weighs as Much as the Sun #shorts
items.description:
Sirius B is 11,270 km across, smaller than Earth, yet it holds the mass of the Sun: 339,000 Earths.
Full video: What If We Swapped the Sun for 5 Other Stars? One Puts Earth INSIDE It

Sources
• Bond et al. 2017 (Astrophysical Journal, Hubble astrometry): Sirius B mass 1.018 solar masses, radius 0.0081 solar radii (about 5,635 km); orbital period about 50 years; Sirius is 8.6 light-years away
• NASA Earth Fact Sheet: Earth mean diameter 12,742 km; 1 solar mass = 332,946 Earth masses
• Own calculations: average density = mass ÷ volume ≈ 2.7 × 10^9 kg/m³, so a 5 mL teaspoon ≈ 13.5 tonnes (an African elephant weighs about 6 tonnes); surface gravity GM/r² ≈ 433,000 × Earth's; Sun's surface gravity ≈ 28 × Earth's, Jupiter's ≈ 2.5 ×
• NASA: the Sun will end its life as a white dwarf

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #stars #whitedwarf
